analysis.investment_thesis: Craftsman Automation is a capital-hungry auto-ancillary conglomerate with D/E of 1.09 and rapidly rising borrowings (₹3,311 Cr in FY25 vs ₹800 Cr in FY22) that is consuming all operating cashflows through capex, leaving FCF at -₹706 Cr in FY25. At 52.2x trailing P/E with ROE of 9.4% and promoter below 50%, this fails every key SMILE metric simultaneously.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 22.8% over 8 years (₹1,102 Cr → ₹5,690 Cr) demonstrates genuine operational scale-up across Powertrain, Aluminium, and Industrial segments
Diversification across CV, 2W, PV, and industrial storage/racking reduces single-customer dependency and creates cross-cycle resilience
Operating cashflow positive all 5 years (₹283–608 Cr range) shows the underlying business generates real cash before capex
key_risks: D/E of 1.09 with borrowings surging to ₹3,311 Cr (FY25) and finance cost of ₹217 Cr consuming 108% of FY25 net profit of ₹201 Cr — debt is eating shareholder returns
Net profit collapsed from ₹337 Cr (FY24) to ₹201 Cr (FY25) despite revenue growing 28% — a massive margin and interest squeeze that questions the investment thesis
FCF of -₹706 Cr in FY25 with capex of ₹992 Cr — the company is in a capital consumption phase with no near-term FCF visibility
red_flags: D/E 1.09 — hard red flag; Kedia's ceiling is 0.4x; at 1.09x this is a leveraged industrial cyclical, not a compounder
Promoter 48.70% — below 50% threshold; majority owner has less than majority stake
P/E 52.2x for a business with 9.4% ROE and declining PAT in FY25 — the market is pricing a recovery that may not materialize as interest costs compound
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Craftsman's story is one of aggressive capacity-led growth — it has nearly quintupled revenue over 8 years by taking on debt and building out machining and casting facilities. The Aluminium Products segment serving EV-adjacent applications is genuinely interesting. But at ₹18,347 Cr market cap, you are paying large-cap valuations for a company that generated only ₹201 Cr PAT in FY25 on ₹5,690 Cr revenue — an alarmingly thin 3.5% net margin.

The FY25 balance sheet is alarming: total assets doubled to ₹8,266 Cr while borrowings swelled to ₹3,311 Cr. Financing CF of +₹1,393 Cr confirms heavy equity/debt raise. This is not a SMILE business — it is a leveraged industrial rollup at a premium multiple with no FCF, below-50% promoter, and returns (ROE 9.4%) below cost of equity. Avoid completely.
